doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Closing questions, local groups, Russ Dantzler and Claude
summary: He enjoyed the music despite bad gigs, hasn't played flute lately, and talks about the Germany tour via Russ Dantzler.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well I’ve been fascinated to talk to you, and is there anything that I haven’t asked you that you’d care to —
Well this about covers it you know. I can’t think of anything else. Of course I worked in many, many small groups, especially in Ohio, they’re all very good groups, local groups.
Do you have any recollection of a gig, or a series of gigs that was just plain a disaster that you couldn’t wait until they were over.
Oh no not really. Because I enjoy playing the music so much. Although there is some things that weren’t too good, but the music overwhelmed all of that.
Well that’s good to hear. Well great. I hope you have a good gig tonight. Did you bring your flute and clarinet with you?
You’re just doing the alto thing, huh?
No I haven’t played flute for a long time. Or clarinet. They asked me to play flute on my next record date. But I haven’t played it for quite a while.
Do you work with Russ Dantzler, out of New York?
Yeah, Russ, yeah. He got me a tour of Germany this year I think it was, or last year. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
Well you’re in good company with him. He’s got Benny Waters.
And the fiddle player, what’s his name?
Claude, yeah. That Claude is scheduled, man, doing every day.
He’s out there. Actually he’s going to be up in our area in November, and I’m going to get to play with him actually, so I’m looking forward to that.
Yeah, okay. Well Claude, he’s almost ninety, isn’t he?
